correctness.rationale: Proposition 2.1 attachment representation is conditioned on: U_j independently uniform among other vertices; root A_j=1{U_j>j}, terminal B_i=product_{j>i}1{U_j!=i}. For j>i, a new root forces U_j>j>i and gives Cov(A_j,B_i)=(n-j)q^(n-i-1)/(n-1)^2; j<=i gives zero. Finite geometric sums establish the exact aggregate (n-2)-(5n-8)q^(n-1)/2. Using independent root Bernoullis and, when nonroots, independent lower-parent choices V_j, deleting a parent edge by turning A_j on cannot reduce terminal count. Product-measure Harris inequality proves all monotone transforms nonnegatively associated; A_2 under an explicit positive-probability parent profile gives strictness. Pair-terminal probabilities and uniform Taylor Riemann sums yield the correlation (e-5/2)*sqrt(6/(e-2)). Fresh independent exhaustive choice-array enumeration n=3..6 checked every cross-kernel entry, moment, all upper-threshold covariances. The asymptotic theorem follows from uniform analytic estimates, not the finite checks.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks are restricted to explicitly stated bounds; infinite assertions rest on inspected analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Bienvenu–Duchamps–Foutel-Rodier derive the stationary attachment construction, root marginal and degree distribution; the precise zero-child terminal definition and root-terminal joint association are a new combination, not identical to total graph-theoretic degree-one count. Random recursive trees and their root-degree/leaf covariances have a different attachment law. Existing representation strongly motivates the result and makes computation possible; unexplored derivative observables remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: Uniform-attachment representation is known; unnoticed prior covariance/association corollaries from the same paper or related forest models could cover part of the result.

value.rationale: Component count and zero-child terminal count are intrinsic, combinatorially meaningful Moran-forest statistics. Their universal increasing association, strictly triangular local influence kernel and persistent nonzero limit correlation supply a structural joint law, sharper than computing an isolated covariance. This distinguishes dependent root/leaf fluctuations in a dynamic forest equilibrium.
